title: Vizing's theorem: chromatic index at most one more than maximum degree
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$, and let $L(G)$ denote its line graph. Then the chromatic number of $L(G)$ — equivalently, the chromatic index (edge chromatic number) $\chi'(G)$ of $G$ — satisfies
\[
\chi(L(G)) \le \Delta(G) + 1.
\]
replaced:
The core content of Vizing, \texttt{$\chi$$'$ $\le$ $\Delta$+1}, from which the
disjunction follows via (6.1).

The book does not state this separately; it is the reduction opening the proof of
Theorem 6.2:

By virtue of (6.1) we need only show that $\chi' \leq \Delta + 1$.
